channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: Malaysia Seeks Details From Anthropic Over AI Influence Campaign
item.description: Malaysia is seeking further details from Anthropic PBC over the alleged use of its artificial intelligence models to power a political influence operation targeting voters in the country.
item.dc:creator: Danial Azhar

item.title: Ambani Seeks to Build Satellite Capacity for Starlink Challenge
item.description: Billionaire Mukesh Ambani-led Reliance Group is exploring manufacturing partnerships to support its planned 1,600-satellite broadband constellation, people familiar with the matter said, in a push to create an Indian-controlled alternative to Elon Musk’s Starlink.
item.dc:creator: Mihir Mishra and P R Sanjai

item.title: Stocks End Lower For A 4th Straight Session, Nvidia Earnings
item.description: Bloomberg Television brings you the latest news and analysis leading up to the final minutes and seconds before and after the closing bell on Wall Street. Today's guests are Tola Capital’s Founder and Managing Director Sheila Gulati, Guggenheim Securities’ Senior Analyst for Retail and eCommerce Simeon Siegel, Sagard’s Chairman, CEO and Co-founder Paul Desmarais III, Darden Restaurants’ Former Chairman and CEO Clarence Otis, Gabelli Funds’ Portfolio Manager and Growth Portfolios John Belton, Science and Technology Partners’ CIO Erika Klauer, New Street Research’s Equity Research Analyst ofTechnology Infrastructure Antoine Chkaiban, Harvard Business School’s Professor of Management Practice Willy Shih, Great Hill Capital’s Chairman Thomas Hayes, Council on Foreign Relations’ Senior Fellow on China and Emerging Technologies Chris McGuire, University of Tennessee at Knoxville’s Supply Chain Management Clinical Associate Professor Sara Hsu (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Nvidia Boosts Forecast, Quashes Huang’s Return
item.description: Nvidia delivered a sales forecast that exceeded Wall Street estimates, signaling that demand remains strong following the chaotic exit of CEO Jensen Huang. Ed Ludlow reports. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Nvidia Stops Selling AI Chips to China Despite US Approval
item.description: Nvidia Corp. is no longer shipping Hopper data center chips to China, despite winning the US government’s blessing to sell a version of that model to the Asian nation last year.
item.dc:creator: Maggie Eastland

item.title: Anthropic Backers Sequoia, Lightspeed Set to Invest More in IPO
item.description: A string of Anthropic PBC’s existing venture capital investors are looking to pour even more money into the artificial intelligence startup in its upcoming initial public offering, a sign of continued fervor and support from firms that have already significantly invested in the company.
item.dc:creator: Natasha Mascarenhas

item.title: Senate Hearing Condemns Roblox’s Child Safety Record
item.description: An 11-year-old boy was tricked into sending explicit photos of himself to a man he met on the gaming platform Roblox. The stranger threatened to share the images with members of an online gaming group, and the boy begged him to delete the photos. Later, the boy confronted the man at his home in Venus, Texas, where he was sexually assaulted.
item.dc:creator: Cecilia D'Anastasio

item.title: Nvidia Does Not Intend to Bring Back Huang as CEO, Chair Says
item.description: Harvey Jones, chair of Nvidia's board, says former CEO Jensen Huang voluntarily resigned and the board does not intend to rehire him. He spoke on the earnings call after Nvidia said sales will increase 75% in fiscal 2028. Jones also talked about the effort to replace Huang. Bloomberg's Ed Ludlow reports. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Microsoft Executive Says Nvidia Drama Could Boost Rival Chips
item.description: Nvidia Corp.’s corporate drama could help prompt customers to consider alternatives to the company’s AI chips, according to a top Microsoft Corp. executive.
item.dc:creator: Brody Ford

item.title: Pushback to OKXICE, Anthropic Perpetual Futures, 'Problem Gamblers'
item.description:
"Bloomberg Crypto" covers the people, transactions, and technology shaping the world of decentralized finance. Today's guests: True Markets Co-Founder and CEO Vishal Gupta, DTCC Digital Assets Managing Director & Global Head Nadine Chakar, and ONDO Katie Managing Director Partnerships Katie Wheeler.
CORRECT: Guest misstated the figure for companies objecting to OKXICE’s plans. Of the 62 companies on OKXICE’s original list, 56 objected. In total, 67 companies objected, including some outside the original list. Data in on-air graphics also corrected. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Nvidia's CEO Issues May Only Be the Tip of the Iceberg, Great Hill's Hayes Says
item.description: Great Hill Capital Chairman Thomas Hayes analyzes Nvidia’s latest earnings report and leadership uncertainty. Speaking on "Bloomberg The Close," Hayes expects a four-to-six month CEO search and an “information vacuum," and expresses skepticism that Jensen Huang will be reinstated. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Tech Paranoia Intensifies After Outages Roil Public Trust
item.description: Technology failures disrupting everything from Americans’ air travel and banking transactions to secretive work at the US National Security Agency are fueling public distrust and paranoia about tech infrastructure — even with no sign the episodes are linked or the work of malicious actors.
item.dc:creator: Jeff Stone, Ryan Gallagher and Jordan Robertson

item.title: Truist Says Tech Stocks Poised to Rebound After Valuation Rout
item.description: Investors who are underweight technology stocks should consider increasing their exposure after a historic decline in valuations and a sharp deterioration in sentiment, according to Truist Advisory Services’ Keith Lerner.
item.dc:creator: Emily Forgash

item.title: Key Takeaways From Nvidia's First Results Since CEO Departure
item.description: Nvidia gave a sales forecast that exceeded Wall Street estimates, signaling that demand remains strong following the chaotic exit of CEO Jensen Huang. Mandeep Singh has more on "Bloomberg The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Nvidia Assures Investors That Company Can Thrive Without Huang
item.description: Nvidia Corp. sought to deliver a clear message during its first earnings update since the departure of longtime leader Jensen Huang: He’s not coming back, and the company will be fine without him.
item.dc:creator: Ian King

item.title: Coatue, Thrive in Talks to Value Ramp Up to $75 Billion
item.description: Ramp is in talks for a new funding round from investors including Coatue Managment and Thrive Capital that could value it at as much as $75 billion, according to people familiar with the matter.
item.dc:creator: Rebecca Torrence

item.title: Trump’s $50 Billion Airspace Upgrade Push Hits Senate Hurdle
item.description: President Donald Trump’s $50.1 billion request to overhaul the US airspace system is hitting resistance in the US Senate, where members of both parties are demanding more details on the administration’s plan to modernize the critical infrastructure after a technology breakdown grounded flights nationwide last week.
item.dc:creator: Allyson Versprille and Erik Wasson

item.title: China Warns US of Retaliation Over New AI Chip Restrictions
item.description: China warned the US it would retaliate if Washington proceeds with curbs on remote access to advanced chips, while urging the Trump administration to resolve differences through dialogue.
item.dc:creator: Foster Wong

item.title: Emerging-Market Currencies Halt Three-Day Slump, Stocks Slide
item.description: Emerging-market currencies rebounded as the dollar halted a five-day rally, while developing stocks retreated for a fourth straight session with Nvidia Corp.’s earnings in focus.
item.dc:creator: Ray Ndlovu and Nicolle Yapur

item.title: Anthropic Faces a Longer Wait Than SpaceX to Join Indexes
item.description: Anthropic’s planned initial public offering could generate billions of dollars in demand from index-tracking funds, though the artificial intelligence startup may have to wait longer than SpaceX did to join two major stock benchmarks.
item.dc:creator: Lu Wang
